answer.sameness: Despite rearranging elements, the set relies on three rigid structural archetypes: an empty typographic grid with massive whitespace (atelje-bergant, urarstvo-tic, plesna-sola-takt), a split screen where the headline sits inside a white box overlapping a right-hand photo (sirarna-pr-simnu, steklarstvo-vrhovnik), and a horizontal banner image stacked directly over a dark colored block (kolesarski-servis-ovinek, vinarstvo-pinteric). Nearly every page uses the exact same tiny rectangular 'Pokličite' button, sparse two-item headers ('Domov' and a single contact link), and an identical 'Ustvarjeno z UI' badge in the top-right corner of every single photograph.
recurringIssues: Several pages (atelje-bergant, urarstvo-tic, plesna-sola-takt) look unfinished on desktop, consisting only of black text floating in vast, unstyled white space.
Sticky mobile bottom action bars crudely cover up body text and section headings on steklarstvo-vrhovnik, sirarna-pr-simnu, and pivovarna-rov.
Desktop navigation headers are bare and utilitarian, lacking proper branding, logos, or complete site menus.
Call-to-action buttons ('Pokličite') are undersized and often float awkwardly detached from the main headline.
The 'Ustvarjeno z UI' watermark badge on every image cheapens the photography and draws attention to artificial assets.
Inconsistent mobile action bars switch arbitrarily between three different button styles and layouts across the set.

best.why: It feels the most like a complete, editorial webpage with a balanced soft-blue palette, well-proportioned typography, and a nice drop-cap detail.
The warm burgundy color scheme, classic serif typography, and overlapping headline box pair naturally with the rustic cheese wheel photography.
The high-contrast black block, bold uppercase sans-serif type, and tight mechanical crop give it an urgent,industrial feel suited to a repair shop.

weakest.why: Anwatchmaker needs visual precision and craft, yet the desktop screen is a barren white void with zero imagery and disconnected text blocks.
For an architectural studio, having no visual work shown on the first screen and an awkward, empty upper-left quadrant looks like a broken wireframe.
The mustard background feels flat and dated, while the tiny, stamp-sized image on the right edge is completely out of scale with the desktop viewport.

answer.oneChange: Eliminate the barren, image-free text layouts and give every business a complete visual art direction—combining authentic, full-scale imagery with proper brand marks and well-proportioned navigation—while fixing the mobile sticky bars so they never collide with page content.
answer.summary: Your studio avoids the trap of using a single rigid template for every client, and your typographic choices generally suit the different trades well. However, the portfolio splits into two problematic extremes: pages that repeat the exact same overlapping-box or stacked-banner tricks, and pages that look like unstyled wireframes floating in empty white space. An architect or watchmaker cannot be represented by a blank white screen with three blocks of text. Furthermore, basic UI polish is lacking: headers feel bare, desktop buttons are tiny, and mobile sticky bars crash directly over body copy. Focus on complete visual art direction for every client and tighten your responsive QA.
